segments.text: This episode is about family members who think they already understand one another, but slowly realize they may have judged too quickly.

segments.text: Phil wants to have a closer relationship with Jay, his father-in-law. He tells Claire that he and Jay are good friends, but Claire points out that after sixteen years of marriage, Phil still acts nervous around him.
segments.tts_text: [a natural conversational storyteller] Phil wants to have a closer relationship with Jay, his father-in-law. He tells Claire that he and Jay are good friends, but Claire points out that after sixteen years of marriage, Phil still acts nervous around him.

segments.text: When Phil visits Jay, Jay is working on a model airplane and clearly wants to be left alone. Phil keeps trying to join in, so Jay finally takes him to a field to fly it. Phil is excited and hopes this will be their chance to connect.
segments.tts_text: [a storyteller building gentle suspense] When Phil visits Jay, Jay is working on a model airplane and clearly wants to be left alone. Phil keeps trying to join in, so Jay finally takes him to a field to fly it. Phil is excited and hopes this will be their chance to connect.

segments.text: At first, things seem to be going well. Then Jay asks Phil to stand far away and hold up a hoop so he can fly the plane through it. Instead, Jay flies the plane straight into Phil’s face.

segments.text: He says it was an accident, but Claire knows her father too well and makes him admit the truth.

segments.text: Jay explains that Phil tries too hard, which gets on his nerves. Claire tells him that Phil only does that because Jay never makes any effort with him. Jay finally apologizes and tells Phil that he likes him. He even says Phil is a good dad, which means a lot to him.

segments.text: Meanwhile, Claire is arguing with her younger daughter, Alex, about what she should wear to a wedding. Claire wants her to wear a dress, but Alex doesn’t want to look like Haley. She feels that Claire doesn’t understand her at all.

segments.text: Gloria takes Alex shopping and talks to her more like a friend than a parent. Alex eventually admits that she doesn’t think she’s pretty like Haley and Claire.

segments.text: Mitchell and Cameron have a much lighter problem. They go to Costco to buy diapers, but Mitchell looks down on the store and wants to leave as quickly as possible. Then he discovers the cheap wine, the food, the electronics, and the huge packs of everything.

segments.text: By the end, Jay makes an effort with Phil, Claire gives Alex more room, and Mitchell admits he was wrong about Costco. Nobody changes completely, but they all understand one another a little better.
